title: Telix Design Proposal
description: Design proposal for Telix, a research operating-system and toolchain architecture. The document covers the system design — memory, scheduling, filesystem, I/O, clustering, control plane, personality, and polyglot language integration (including a GHC cross-compilation target and a musl libc port) — together with an adversary model and TCB decomposition, isolation primitives, an explicit degradation path, a comparison against seven contemporary systems with the five claims claimed as novel, and a three-tier structure for empirical validation (inherited evidence, the page-clustering performance hypothesis, and compositional burden). Claims without prototype evidence are labelled as hypotheses; the design-review note tracking objections is kept out of the frozen artifact.
